theory.intro: Data can be shown in a table, a column graph or a line graph. You can read single values and also combine them to find totals.
facts: A **table** lists each category with its value; a **column graph** shows each value as a bar height.
To find a **total**, add the values of all categories together.
Always check the scale of a graph — one step may be worth more than $1$.
steps: Read the value for each category from the table or bar height.
For a total, add every value together.
For a difference, subtract the smaller value from the larger.

foundation.question_text: The table shows visitors to community rooms. How many visited the Games room? $\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Room}&\text{Craft}&\text{Games}&\text{Study}&\text{Music}\\\hline\text{Visitors}&18&27&14&21\end{array}$
Find the total number of meals delivered. $\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Day}&\text{Mon}&\text{Tue}&\text{Wed}&\text{Thu}\\\hline\text{Meals}&32&28&35&25\end{array}$
How many more parcels did Route B deliver than Route D? $\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Route}&A&B&C&D\\\hline\text{Parcels}&45&62&38&27\end{array}$

development.question_text: The total attendance was $150$. Find the missing Friday value. $\begin{array}{c|rrrrr}\text{Day}&\text{Mon}&\text{Tue}&\text{Wed}&\text{Thu}&\text{Fri}\\\hline\text{Attendance}&26&31&29&34&?\end{array}$

development.solution_text:
The three largest values are $60$, $50$ and $40$.
$60+50+40$
$=150\text{ memberships}$

development.question_text: A food bank packed $184$ boxes in total. Use the table to find how many were Vegetable boxes. $\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Box type}&\text{Fruit}&\text{Dry}&\text{Chilled}&\text{Vegetable}\\\hline\text{Boxes}&46&58&35&?\end{array}$

development.solution_text:
$40+60=100$
Clinic C has $120$ visits.
$120-100$
$=20$
Clinics A and D together have $20$ fewer visits than Clinic C.

development.question_text: A transport desk records enquiries. Find the difference between the total morning and afternoon enquiries. $\begin{array}{c|rrr} &\text{Bus}&\text{Train}&\text{Ferry}\\\hline\text{Morning}&24&31&15\\\text{Afternoon}&18&27&20\end{array}$

mastery.question_text: The total is $255$. Find the missing values when C is $20$ more than D. $\begin{array}{c|rrrr}\text{Category}&A&B&C&D\\\hline\text{Value}&45&50&?&?\end{array}$
mastery.solution_text:
$255-(45+50)=160$
The two missing values total $160$ and differ by $20$.
$D=(160-20)\div2=70$
$C=70+20=90$

mastery.question_text: A column graph shows $45$, $75$, $30$, $60$ and $90$ visits. A report excludes the largest category. What total should the report give?
A table lists $18$, $27$ and $35$ calls. A line graph for three different hours shows $20$, $25$ and $30$ calls. Which display has the larger total, and by how much?
mastery.solution_text:
$18+27+35=80$
$20+25+30=75$
$80-75$
$=5\text{ calls}$
The table has the larger total by $5$ calls.
